notes:
- Depth Lighting's Strength runs from -100 to 100 instead of -200 to 200, and is 50% stronger at every point of the slider: the top now gives three times the light, where 200 gave twice it. Lights you already set keep their place on the slider and get the extra strength.
- **Cancel stitch** stops a panorama while it stitches, as Cancel merge stops a stack, within a moment even at full size, and **Stitch again** picks it up when you want it.
- Recolor's Neutral guard shows how colorful the photograph is and how much of it the Hue rows reach, and when a Hue curve barely changes a muted photograph it offers the guard that lets the edit land.
- Selections, crop handles, gradient handles, the straighten line, layer Transform and Warp handles and brush strokes keep going when the pointer leaves the canvas, until you let go, and a selection can begin on the gray around the photograph.
- A panorama of phone DNGs opens without the RAW Tone Profile as soon as it is made, not only after the folder is opened again.
- A baked DNG whose picture is mostly fine grain, such as a max stack of hundreds of night frames, opens again; it was taken for a decoding failure and the canvas could not show it.
- A stack or panorama of JPEGs opens with the Tone Profile off, as a single JPEG does, instead of with Heeler's RAW look added on top of the camera's. It looked over-saturated, and baking it kept that look. The same goes for DNGs baked by Heeler, and in a panorama for phone DNGs that carry their own rendering, mixed with JPEGs or not.
- A DNG baked by Heeler is also marked as finished in its XMP metadata, so it still opens with the Tone Profile off after another program rewrites its metadata.
- A panorama's full-size export uses the same frames as its preview. It could leave frames out, and with them part of the view, without saying so.
- Changing the method, frames or settings of a stack or panorama you stopped merges or stitches it again with the new settings.
- Baking a stack that has to merge first closes the Bake dialog and shows the merge's progress, then the bake's, instead of the merge's card half hidden behind the dialog. Bake to Image now has a progress dialog with Cancel.
- The ribbon says how many photographs are selected when two or more are.
- Panorama stitching shows its progress the way a stack merge does: how many frames, the stage, how far along and about how long is left.
- Merge to HDR without exposure information (JPEGs with no EXIF) gives the same result whatever order the frames are in, and repeating detail in the scene no longer throws off its exposure estimate.
- The Stack panel says when an HDR merge is approximate: frames that are JPEGs or other finished pictures still carry the camera's tone curve, so merge the RAW files for an accurate result.
- Merge to Median with an even number of frames takes the average of the two middle values. Two frames used to merge to the brighter of each pair, the same picture as Light Trails, and four or six leaned bright.
- The eyedroppers on Recolor's curves and the Black & White hue curve add a point where you click, as Curves and Recolor's Depth row already did, and holding the click drags that new point up or down. A quick click on the hue curve adds its point too.
- Relight's eyedropper adds a point on its curve where you click, and holding the click drags it. Before, dragging after a pick did nothing on most photographs.
- A curve eyedropper's point lands where its ghost showed: the hover and the click read the same patch of the picture, and a click on a gray spot drops its point where the ghost holds the last hue. Relight's eyedropper shows its ghost too.
- Source has a **Tone profile** switch. A JPEG, a bake or a phone DNG opens with the profile off, and Source used to show its controls anyway, doing nothing.
- Relight's eyedropper and Recolor's Around rows place their point at the tone or color the adjustment actually works on there, not at the single pixel under the pointer.
- Every curve eyedropper takes a point already there when the click is within 1% of it; Curves took 1.5%, and on Curves that click now selects the point so a held drag moves it.
- Adding a Lens Character flare keeps a single Depth Lighting light from an older version instead of replacing it.
- Dragging a point with the Black & White hue curve's eyedropper no longer brings back the hover marker at a hue the cursor has left.
- The eyedropper previews in Color Sets, Black & White and Recolor no longer slip back to an older hue when the app is busy; they stay on the hue under the cursor.
- Pressing Escape in the middle of a crop or other tool's drag no longer leaves Recolor's Neutral guard strip, Polish and the depth tools waiting for another drag before they update.
- A Depth Lighting light, a color chart's corner or the divider between panels no longer follows the pointer after you switch to another app in the middle of dragging it.
